consequences: The inspector remains integrated in the existing main window; this does not claim the separate inspector-window or complete L3/L4/Frame-content/replay/export targets. Client wait uses the existing90-second Host transport limit, not a provider abort guarantee. Audits store scope hashes, preview hash, result and rollback status; uncertain effects stay open for review.
context: The accepted Desktop PRD revision134 requires typed preview/execute, idempotency, expected revision, short process/profile/window-scoped debug capabilities and audit. The current console only lists real admin specs; generic execute can duplicate effects before recording completion.
decision: Expose seven explicitly adapted L1 maintenance commands through five-minute child capabilities opened by the Rust main-window broker. Keep all capability tokens native-only, enforce profile/owner/origin/client scope, schema validation, preview fingerprints and durable actor/request-key preview identity. Claim execution before handler entry; unknown effects are never retried automatically. Permit same-profile redacted audit reads across process restarts, but only the originating client may execute its preview. Keep unadapted schemas and minimum levels unknown, and data/force/filesystem/L4 actions disabled.
title: Native scoped maintenance command broker
